To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amount of time students spend in different types of literacy instruction, covering specific content, and the quality of the global classroom learning environment interact to predict students' vocabulary and reading outcomes.

the global quality of a classroom's learning environment and the time individual students spend in specific types of instruction on specific content synergistically predict students' vocabulary and comprehension gains.
the amount of time students spent in literacy activities and quality of the learning environment synergistically predicted students' literacy gains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the complex interactions between classroom learning environments and the literacy instruction children receive.
the complex interactions among students' individual characteristics, classroom processes, and outcomes.
the development of a dynamic, systems approach to classroom assessment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the classroom learning environment interacts with the content and type of instruction to predict students' vocabulary and reading outcomes.

both the quality of the learning environment and the amount of time students spent in literacy activities were important for vocabulary and comprehension outcomes and that these effects were not independent of one another.
the quality of the learning environment and the amount of time spent in specific types literacy instruction interacted to predict third grade students' vocabulary and reading gains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the more time students spend in literacy instruction, the more likely they are to improve in reading comprehension and vocabulary, especially when the instruction is focused on specific content areas and the teacher is in a directive role (e.g., teaching, demonstrating, and leading) rather than a responsive role (e.g, listening, asking questions, and providing feedback).
classrooms are complex systems, and that both the quality of the learning environment and the type and content of instruction are important in predicting students' vocabulary and reading outcomes.

the quality of a classroom environment and the time spent in different types of instruction are both important for student outcomes, but the effects of these two factors interact with each other in complex ways to affect student outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to move beyond a simple focus on time in literacy instruction and the global quality of instruction in the classroom to understand how children learn in classrooms.
we can better predict students' learning when we look at the complexity of the classroom environment.
classroom learning environments and instruction interact to affect student outcomes and that the quality of the learning environment is a critical component of instruction.
